summary: Backend startup readiness fix verification - All 8 tests passed. The fix correctly addresses the production deployment issue where nginx health checks were getting connection refused.
test_credentials: N/A - no auth required for this test
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend startup readiness fix verified. The fix ensures /health is available immediately at startup while heavy router registration runs in background.

verified_fix_details.issue: Production deployment failed readiness because nginx health checks to /health on 127.0.0.1:8001 got connection refused. Old live version remained visible.
verified_fix_details.root_cause: register_all_routers(app) was being called at module import time, blocking the import path and delaying /health availability.

fix_applied.1_import_not_blocking: register_all_routers(app) is now only imported, NOT called at module level
fix_applied.2_health_defined_early: /health endpoint is defined directly on app at module level (line 782-790)
fix_applied.3_background_bootstrap: _bootstrap_worker_routes_and_tasks() is scheduled via asyncio.create_task() in startup_event()
fix_applied.4_startup_guard: startup_guard_middleware allows /health even during 'booting' or 'routes_loading' states

verification_results.health_at_import: True - /health route present immediately after import
verification_results.routes_at_import: < 20 routes (only health, root, pay.js, static mounts)

tests_executed.name: test_health_route_present_at_import
tests_executed.description: /health route exists immediately after module import

tests_executed.name: test_register_all_routers_not_called_at_import
tests_executed.description: Only ~10 routes at import (not 200+), confirming routers not loaded at import

tests_executed.name: test_server_py_structure
tests_executed.description: Code structure matches expected fix pattern

production_deployment_assessment.explanation: The fix ensures /health is available within ~0.4s of uvicorn loading the module. Heavy router registration (200+ routes) now runs in background after startup. This means nginx health checks will succeed quickly, allowing the new deployment to become ready and replace the old live version.
production_deployment_assessment.recommendation: The fix should resolve the production deployment readiness issue. The 40s start-period in Dockerfile provides ample time for the fast import (~0.4s) plus any container startup overhead.

test_scope: Backend Only - Startup Readiness Fix Verification
